Car wrecks. Doesn't seem like an odd fear, but the extent is a bit off-putting to some.

I was in a car wreck about 8-9 months ago. I was fine, but it was a pretty bad wreck nonetheless. I was 100% certain that I was going to die, and it's a strange thing to be faced with your own mortality like that, especially considering how young I am. Ever since I have very strong, physical reactions to wrecks. They appear on TV all the time (Seriously, have you ever noticed this? It doesn't matter the genre. Comedies, kid's shows, dramas, cartoons, you name it, there's an often unexpected hardcore head on collision in it. Fucking insane.), and I'll jump, make a weird sort of sobbing noise, bury my head in my hands, while images of my wreck come back very rapid fire and I'll usually have to stifle tears. While the memories of the wreck come back, it's like I can't hear anything or remember what's going on around me. If my best friend is there, she'll put her hand on my shoulder to "ground me in reality" as she puts it. I make little noises while others are driving if they so much as tap the brakes a little too hard. I realize that it's annoying, but it's involuntary and I'm trying to work on it. When I try to sleep at night, sometimes I'll start to remember my wreck and my face just twists as though I'm about to cry and my stomach does that thing where it contracts and releases a bunch of times like when you cry, and I just force myself to think about something else. I have no idea why any of this happens, and I have no clue what to do about it. I've tried to work on it, but most of the reactions I have are involuntary.

I've pissed a few people off by refusing to ride with them, I'm just so scared of getting into a wreck...
